direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is very fun, acting as a love letter to the golden era of Hollywood with homages and using the Illumination animation style to create old Hollywood references while maintaining the physical comedy and action sequences of a classic Minion movie; The microscale is very much Minion, so if you turn your brain off, it is very fun; Storytelling is fine, presenting a very basic story where you shouldn't look too deeply into the plot

performance.comments: Wears many hats cause he not only is the director, but voices all the minions, and given that the entire movie is basically in Minionese, he really carries the movie with the minions as they are very adorable and silly, using their gibberish sliced in with real words in English, Spanish, and French to make their physical comedy shine
Basically just uses his Member Berries voice from South Park, but it's nice to see he is in other projects besides South Park because he is genuinely a very good voice actor and it shows on screen
Basically the narrator and uses her actual voice
Seems to be having fun and is able to play a little despite his role being pretty well defined
Feels a bit out of place, but I am happy he's getting his bag and that's what matters most
Is allowed to play a little bit and it is nice to see he is playing two roles, but his role is pretty defined
Kinda is just in the movie

cast.comments: Everyone seemed like they were having fun making this, not really the best chemistry, but its not really needed as most of the movie is just Coffin's Minion characters talking to themselves

story.comments: For a seventh Despicable Me/Minion movie, they found a way to make this movie fresh because the concept is a love letter to cinema; The plot structure uses a Princess Bride-style retelling framing device with an A-plot and a B-plot—while the B-plot is just okay, the A-plot is what really pays the bills; The character writing is silly and adorable, making this movie a fun watch as you empathize with and care for these Minions

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is almost entirely in Minionese, but this movie is really a lesson in the language because, by the end of it, you understand about 60% of what they are saying, as it's just gibberish with real English, Spanish, and French words spliced in; The movie being entirely in Minionese adds to the comedy because it's really fun if you turn your brain off; The movie also relies on physical comedy, which is very smart because it takes place at the turn of cinema from the silent movie era to the talkies; Many of the jokes also reference the history of cinema and older movies, which helps add to the humor, especially if you pick up on the references; The symbolism involves many allusions to the origins of Hollywood and other older films, as they basically recreate these movies in the Illumination style while adding the Minions as the subject; The symbolism is also surprisingly strong, as the movie takes place during the transition from the silent era to the talkies, mirroring how the Minions are masters of silent physical comedy but have to reinvent themselves when the talkies arrive; The foreshadowing is what you would expect for a family animated movie

score.comments: The score works great alongside the soundtrack to recreate the era and transport you back to Old Hollywood and the Roaring '20s

soundtrack.comments: The soundtrack helps transport you right back to Old Hollywood and the Roaring '20s

editing.comments: The editing helps add to the charm of this movie by highlighting and splicing in the homages, giving it a very old-timey, vintage Hollywood feel at times

sound.comments: The sound uses a lot of older sound effects to help amplify the homages to Old Hollywood

animation.comments: While it is generally a generic Illumination animation style, I loved how they used it to recreate iconic Old Hollywood movies like Citizen Kane, A Trip to the Moon, and Train coming to the Station in the Minion/Illumination style; It was also fun to see them do E.T., The Matrix, and George Lucas in the Illumination style as well

review.pacing: The pacing is pretty good for the most part; It slows down a bit in the last 40 minutes, where you could probably cut five to ten minutes by shortening the B-plot, even though it is already a short 90-minute movie
review.climax: The climax is a very generic Despicable Me Minion climax that isn't groundbreaking, but it is very fun; The ending ties the movie together very well
review.tone: The tone is like every other movie in this franchise: pretty silly and adorable fun that, if you turn your brain off, is a fun watch overall
review.overall: Overall, 'Minions & Monsters' is genuinely a good movie and the best in the franchise, as it's a fresh and adorable love letter to the history of cinema in Minionese; the movie's constant homages to the golden age of Hollywood in the Illumination style, and the fact that the Minions are the masters of physical comedy at the turn of cinema from the silent era to the advent of sound, make this a surprisingly profound movie that not only families but also cinephiles will enjoy
